title: Priority decomposition and response scripts for log redaction, retention and audit export requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Customers frequently request dataset- or tenant-scoped changes to logging behavior (redaction of sensitive fields, longer/shorter retention windows, and ad-hoc audit exports). Currently intake is ad-hoc across support, SEs, and CSMs which leads to inconsistent SLAs and duplicate work between Product, Security, and Legal.

Objective:
Create a single async triage and prioritization playbook that: 
- Classifies inbound non-bug data-governance requests (redaction, retention, PII handling, audit exports).
- Provides deterministic priority decomposition and SLAs for responses and resolution (including automation vs manual work).
- Supplies templated response scripts and reviewer checklists for Support/SE/CSM to reduce time-to-first-response and ensure correct routing to Product, Security, or Legal.

Scope:
- Included: tenant/scoped logging redaction requests, retention period changes, PII masking requests, export / ad-hoc audit data extraction requests, and requests for export delivery formats (CSV/Parquet/Signed link).
- Excluded: product defects (bug triage), infrastructure incidents, customer-managed on-prem appliance upgrades, or long-term platform design changes that require roadmap allocation (those get a separate RFC).

Proposed triage bands and SLAs:
- Urgent (P0 customer-impacting): data exfiltration risk, legal hold, regulatory investigations. SLA: 4h first response; 24-72h resolution or formal escalation.
- High (P1): requests to redact confirmed PII or remove logs from shared analytics. SLA: 24h first response; 7 business days resolution plan.
- Medium (P2): retention window adjustments, non-sensitive export requests, format changes. SLA: 48h first response; 14 business days implementation or scheduled work.
- Low (P3): informational requests, guidance, best-practice documentation asks. SLA: 72h first response; include self-serve doc or FAQ.

Routing rules (summary):
- If request involves legal/regulatory demand, route immediately to Legal + Security and mark Urgent.
- If request requires code-path changes to runtime (KV cache modifications, kernel-level redaction), route to Engineering + Product and estimate impact.
- If request can be satisfied by configuration changes (rollout-level retention, masking toggles), route to Customer Success/Support with templated steps and automation playbooks.

Templated response scripts (for Support/SE/CSM):
- Acknowledge and classification script (first contact): "Thanks — we received your request to [redact/export/adjust retention]. Can you confirm the tenant ID, example log lines (redacted), and whether this is under a legal/regulatory hold? Based on that info we will classify priority and provide next steps within [SLA band]."
- Next-step checklist (for P1/P0): data access freeze, evidence capture, Legal contact, temporary export hold.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc published in Confluence with clear classification table and example request templates.
- Three templated response scripts (P0, P1, P2) added to Support playbook and verified by Support and SE review.
- Routing automation stubbed: a triage form that tags requests by classification and auto-assigns to queue (Legal/Security/Product/CS).
- Two internal runbook checklists produced (Engineering change path; Config-only change path).
- Dashboardable metrics defined (mean time to first response, route accuracy, percent automated) and wire framed in the Console.

Deliverables:
- Confluence playbook: intake form, classification matrix, response scripts, and escalation matrix.
- Jira/Linear templates for each triage band with required fields.
- Support/SE training session and recorded walkthrough.
- Minimal prototype of intake form that tags requests and assigns to correct Slack channel.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Automation vs human review: initial scope favors semi-automated classification (forms + manual review) to avoid misclassification of legal requests.
- SLA targets: recommended bands above are conservative; Product may tighten for enterprise SLA customers after telemetry baseline.
- Data removal vs logical redaction: for many customers logical masking meets needs and is lower-risk, but some regulated requests will require immutable deletion; we need Legal input on retention obligations.

Implementation notes for Eng/Product:
- Create a small set of config knobs in Console for per-tenant retention and masking where feasible (feature flag behind enterprise plan).
- Engineering runbook must include steps for safe backfill removal and auditing (DB queries, indexing impact, and KV cache invalidation).
- Add audit log entries for every triage action and export deliverable (who, what, why).

Success metrics:
- 90% of requests receive first response within SLA bands in 30 days post-launch.
- Reduce escalations to Legal for non-legal issues by 40% (via better routing).
- 50% of incoming requests routed to config-only resolution within 60 days via templated processes.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: misrouted legal/regulatory requests -> Mitigation: mandatory legal flag on form + checklist to escalate.
- Risk: engineering latency from ad-hoc deletions -> Mitigation: restrict destructive operations to scheduled windows + require Security signoff.

- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GOV/triage-playbook-draft
- Intake form prototype (Google Forms): https://docs.google.com/forms/d/proto-logs-intake
- GH PR proto for automated tagging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/421
- Dashboard mock (notion): https://app.notion.so/redwood/triage-dashboard-mock
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with classification matrix and example templates
Support and SE confirm and sign off on three response scripts
Prototype intake form tags and auto-assigns to queues for at least two request types
Engineering and Security have runbook checklists for config-only and code-change paths
Metrics defined and an initial dashboard wireframe completed
